ちなみに日本でやるならツールはこの使い分け

①企業・クリニックの本格サイト→STUDIO
デザイン自由度が高くてCMS付きだから
納品後に顧客が自分でお知らせを更新できる

②単発のLP→ペライチ
最速で形になるから5万円案件はこれで十分

③更新不要の一枚物→Claudeで直接コード生成
VercelやCloudflare Pagesに無料で公開すれば
原価ほぼゼロで利益率が最も高い

この副業がいい理由は
単価が高いこと

ショート動画やブログは再生数、クリック、広告単価を待つしかないけど
ホームページ制作は1件受けるだけでまとまった現金がすぐ入る

これを見て
「AIが30分で勝手に30万円稼いでくれる」
と思うのはNGで、

本当にお金が付くポイントは
ホームページ制作より営業に近い

この人の案件獲得はこの流れ

クモン（韓国版ココナラ）に商品を出して
Imwebでポートフォリオを積んで
インスタのリールで制作事例を見せて
問い合わせが来たら相談して契約に変える

結局AIは制作時間を短縮する道具で
お金は顧客の問題を解決した時に出てくる構造

この事例の良さは
AI副業の中でも成果物がかなり明確な点

ホームページは社長の立場から見て
「今すぐ必要」な人がいる

クリニック
旅館・民泊
清掃業者
小規模事業者
フリーランス
学習塾

こういう所は今でもホームページやLPを必要としている

AIが上手い人と
AIで稼げる人は別物で

稼げるのは「成果物を相手に届けて終わらせられる人」だけ

だからAI副業の良し悪しは
ツールの性能じゃ判断できない

見るべきは3つ

・財布を開くのは誰か
・その人は何に困ってるのか
・納品した後も面倒を見切れるか

ここが描けない副業は何を使っても稼げない

実績ゼロのうちは
安く受けて事例を貯めるのが最短ルート

更に詳細が気になる場合は画像内で分かるYouTube動画を見ると良い

posts.title: Anthropic Just Changed The Rules
posts.content:
Everyone is talking about Claude Fable 5.

I think they're looking at the wrong launch.

Because hidden inside Anthropic's announcement is one sentence that changes everything:

Claude Fable 5 and Claude Mythos 5 are the same underlying model.

Same intelligence.

Same reasoning engine.

Same frontier capabilities.

Different access.

And once you realize that, the entire launch starts looking very different.

Most people think Anthropic launched a new AI model.

What they actually launched was a new idea:

The future of AI may no longer be about who can build the smartest model.

It may be about who gets access to it.

For the last few years, frontier AI followed a simple pattern.

A company trained a more powerful model.

Then eventually everyone got access.

GPT-2 became GPT-3.

GPT-3 became GPT-4.

Claude became Sonnet.

Sonnet became Opus.

Capability increased.

Availability followed.

Fable 5 breaks that pattern.

Anthropic publicly released Fable 5.

But behind Fable sits Mythos 5.

A capability tier above Opus.

A model powerful enough that Anthropic built an entirely separate access program around it.

And here's the interesting part:

The difference isn't intelligence.

The difference is safeguards.

That distinction might become one of the most important developments in modern AI.

Because it suggests we've entered an era where intelligence itself is no longer the product.

Access is.

Most launch coverage focused on benchmarks.

And to be fair, the benchmarks are ridiculous.

SWE-Bench Pro:

• Fable 5 → 80.3%
• Opus 4.8 → 69.2%
• GPT-5.5 → 58.6%

FrontierCode:

• Fable 5 → 29.3%
• Opus 4.8 → 13.4%
• GPT-5.5 → 5.7%

Those are not incremental improvements.

Those are category shifts.

Especially FrontierCode.

The hardest coding benchmark in the announcement shows Fable more than doubling Opus 4.8.

That's not a model getting slightly better.

That's a model operating in a different league.

But even those benchmarks aren't the most interesting part.

The most interesting part is what Anthropic chose to hide behind safeguards.

Cybersecurity.

Biology.

Chemistry.

Model distillation.

Whenever Fable enters those domains, Anthropic's classifiers can automatically route requests to Opus 4.8 instead.

Write prompts.

Generate code.

Repeat.

• Claude reviews every PR automatically

• Documentation updates itself

• Tests run before changes are committed

• Specialized agents handle frontend, backend, and debugging separately

• GitHub, databases, APIs, and cloud infrastructure become directly accessible

At that point, you're not chatting with AI anymore.

You're coordinating an AI-powered development environment.

That's a completely different paradigm.

The biggest shift in AI right now isn't happening at the model layer.

It's happening at the infrastructure layer.

We're moving from:

AI that answers questions

→

AI that participates in systems

And the developers who understand this early will have a massive advantage.

Because the future won't belong to the people writing the best prompts.

Browser automation as we know it is over

The use cases are wild:

→ Ship an AI copilot inside your SaaS in literally lines of code
→ Collapse 20-click ERP/CRM workflows into a single sentence
→ Give any legacy web app voice + natural language control
→ Extend it across tabs with the optional Chrome extension, or drive it externally via MCP

12k+ stars. MIT licensed. Built on browser-use internals — with zero setup overhead.

Everyone's been debating what "AI-native UX" means.

This is what it looks like shipped.

「生成AIを使って、企業課題に対してこういう提案・開発をしました。」
と学生のうちに言えるのは、強いですね。

posts.content:
Underrated number most founders ignore:

What is each department's cost as a % of revenue?

Most know the dollar amount but not the percentage... you need both. A $50k/month marketing budget might be perfectly healthy in one business and a disaster in another.

Example: ad spend for an investment advisory should run 7-12% of revenue. For an info business it’s 30-50%.

The fastest way to find silent killers in your business is to compare that number for each department against your industry’s benchmark.

Almost every industry has one that shocks the hell out of you when you find it.

posts.title: The Only Moat Left In Business Right Now
posts.content:
A founder I work with runs a $180K/month consulting business.
Last year, a competitor launched almost the exact same offer.
Used the same positioning, same price point, and roughly the same promise.
Within 90 days, my founder had signed 14 new clients.  The competitor had signed 2.
It was pretty much the same offer.  Completely opposite result.
The difference was the audience.
My founder had spent 18 months building a personal brand.
He consistently showed up, shared his thinking, and became someone his market actually knew and trusted.
AI has made it trivially easy to clone an offer, reverse-engineer a funnel, and replicate a system.
What it can't do is manufacture the trust that comes from 50,000 people who have followed your thinking and personality for two years.
That's the only real moat left.
And most founders are still treating it like a nice-to-have.
The founders winning right now are the ones owning their distribution.
It makes them impossible to unseat.
The problem I hear from most founders doing $50K–$200K/month is the same:
They know they need to build a personal brand.
But content takes 10 hours a week they don't have.
Hiring a team to do it takes months to figure out.
And every time they sit down to work on it, something more urgent takes over.
So it stays on the "important but not urgent" list.
Meanwhile, the window to own their category organically keeps closing.
